panels.title: FUSE ops/s
panels.description: Total FUSE request rate (all types). NOTE: read requests are split by the kernel into ~256KB chunks (measured p50 249KB from 1MiB app reads), so this does not equal the application's IO operation count.

panels.title: S3 API req/s
panels.description: Measured cross-check: 63 req/s UploadPart x 8MiB part = 504 MB/s, matching FUSE write throughput exactly -> default --write-part-size 8388608 with no retry waste.

panels.title: Throughput (FUSE layer only)
panels.description: !! NOT application throughput. Page-cache hits never reach FUSE, so this UNDER-REPORTS by a varying factor: measured 6.8x low in a cache-friendly read-only run (64 MB/s here vs 437 MB/s in fio) and 1.7x low under mixed read+write (474 MB/s here vs ~787 MB/s app-side). The gap tracks cache hit rate, so treat it as a floor, never as the capacity-planning number.

panels.title: FUSE errors/s (app-visible)
panels.description: HIGHEST-SIGNAL error metric: a non-zero value means the application actually received an I/O error. Stayed at 0 through the entire 2026-07-27 load test even while the S3 layer showed transient events (Mountpoint retried them all).

panels.title: S3 real errors/s
panels.description: Excludes http_status 404 and -1, both of which are NORMAL behaviour (404 = O_CREAT existence probe; -1 = Mountpoint cancelling a duplicate lookup). Only 5xx / throttling / genuine failures land here.

panels.title: Mountpoint RSS
panels.description: Measured growth: 80MB idle -> 617MB write -> 978MB read on a 7.8GB c6i.xlarge (12x). Reads cost more memory than writes. Watch for OOM on small instances.

panels.title: S3 benign events by status (404 = O_CREAT probe, -1 = cancelled dup lookup)
panels.description: Counted in s3_request_errors_total but NOT failures. Verified with --debug --debug-crt on 2026-07-27: 149x CRT 14343 (all response status=404) + 19x CRT 14347 AWS_ERROR_S3_CANCELED 'Request successfully cancelled' (all HeadObject, 0 UploadPart). All 42,865 UploadPart calls returned 200.

panels.title: S3 bottleneck indicator — TOTAL p99 / TTFB p99
panels.description: Ratio ~1 => S3/network is the bottleneck. Ratio >> 1 => TTFB is fine but the body transfer is slow, i.e. LOCAL bandwidth/concurrency limit, NOT S3 being slow. Measured 2026-07-27: UploadPart 9.8x (TTFB 138ms vs TOTAL 1.34s), GetObject 26.1x. Without this ratio the natural (wrong) conclusion is 'S3 got slower'.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (s3_request) (rate(s3_request_total_latency_microseconds[$__rate_interval]))) / histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (s3_request) (rate(s3_request_first_byte_latency_microseconds[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: FUSE latency distribution — heatmap (all requests)
panels.description: Native-histogram bucket distribution over time. Bright = where latency concentrates. Measured under load this is clearly BIMODAL: a dense band at 128us-1ms plus sparse points out past 300ms.

panels.title: FUSE latency percentiles (all requests)
panels.description: True quantiles from exponential histogram buckets. Measured heavy write: p50 250us / p99 213,634us (855x). Measured mixed read+write: p50 64us / p90 311us / p99 23,947us / p99.9 390,052us / p99.99 1,226,967us -> p99.99 is 19,231x p50. The mean is hidden by default: it read 1,670us vs a p50 of 64us (26x inflated by the tail), i.e. it describes neither the typical nor the worst request.

panels.title: FUSE p99 latency by request type
panels.description: LOG AXIS is mandatory: measured 11 op types spanning 5 decades in one chart (releasedir 26us / release 57us / opendir 1,327us / getattr 1,384us / read 13,742us / mknod 14,116us / write 46,669us / readdirplus 169,685us / open 557,957us / lookup 616,637us / flush 1,931,987us) -- a 74,307x spread. On a linear axis eight of these collapse onto the zero line and look perfectly flat.

panels.title: FUSE time contribution by request type (where wall-clock actually goes)
panels.description: histogram_sum, NOT histogram_count: total microseconds spent per op type. Added because ops/s is misleading about importance. Measured under mixed load: read 4,042,068 us/s (66% of time, 2932 ops/s) but flush 673,281 us/s (11% of time from only 0.5 ops/s = 0.017% of requests). flush is the classic case a count-weighted average dilutes into invisibility.

panels.title: FUSE ops/s by request type
panels.description: Request COUNT only -- do not infer importance from this. Measured under mixed load: read 2932 ops/s and write 259 ops/s vs flush 0.5 ops/s, yet flush still burns 11% of all wall-clock time (0.017% of requests). Always pair with the time-contribution panel above.

panels.title: FUSE write latency — heatmap
panels.description: Measured: write p50 barely moves with load (261us light -> 254us heavy, data is buffered) while p99 explodes 304us -> 140,680us when the buffer periodically fills.

panels.title: FUSE flush latency — heatmap (close() waiting on CompleteMultipartUpload)
panels.description: flush is the slowest FUSE op (measured p99 2.13s under load, still 156ms when nearly idle). It is inherent to S3 object semantics: close() must wait for the multipart upload to complete. Applications doing frequent open/close of small files experience SECONDS of latency, not the 185ms that 'write' suggests.

panels.title: FUSE IO size distribution — heatmap
panels.description: Bytes per FUSE request. Reveals small-IO vs large-IO workload mix.

panels.title: FUSE IO size percentiles
panels.description: FUSE-visible size != application request size. Writes pass through 1:1 (avg 1024KB from 1MiB app writes). READS get split/merged by the kernel and the amount VARIES with app block size and concurrency -- measured p50 249KB / avg 213KB for a single 1MiB sequential reader, but p50 4KB / avg 74KB once a 64K reader and concurrent writers were added. Never assume the app's bs value here, and do not treat any single ratio as a constant.

panels.title: Throughput by FUSE request type
panels.description: FUSE-layer bytes only; excludes page-cache hits (see Overview note).

panels.title: Avg IO size by request type
S3 first-byte latency (TTFB) — heatmap
panels.description: Time from S3 request start until first byte received. This reflects S3 server-side responsiveness. Measured: barely changed between light and heavy load (UploadPart 158ms -> 138ms), i.e. S3 did NOT degrade.

panels.title: S3 total latency — heatmap
panels.description: Full request duration including body transfer. Measured heavy write: UploadPart TOTAL p99 1.34s vs TTFB p99 138ms -> the extra ~1.2s is spent pushing the 8MB body over the wire (local bandwidth), not waiting on S3.

panels.title: S3 total latency percentiles by API
S3 request rate by API
panels.description: Per-API S3 call rate. Watch multipart quartet CreateMPU/UploadPart/CompleteMPU: on healthy writes they rise together with DeleteObject≈0. DeleteObject rising in lockstep = create-then-delete waste (see Write Amplification row).

panels.title: S3 errors by API / HTTP status (full breakdown incl. benign)
panels.description: Keep the http_status breakdown -- this is the panel that prevents misdiagnosis. 404 and -1 are benign (see Overview). Real trouble looks like 503 (SlowDown -> reduce concurrency / spread prefixes) or other 5xx.

panels.title: FUSE worker thread pool (--max-threads default 16)
panels.description: Idle threads near 0 = FUSE thread pool saturated -> raise --max-threads. Measured avg idle: 14.0 write-only, 10.4 read-only, 11.0 mixed read+write. p1 idle (worst case) is the line that matters: it hit 4.0 under mixed load (alert threshold is 3) while avg still read a comfortable 11.0 -- the average hides transient saturation. NOTE: queried WITHOUT rate() -- idle_threads is an instantaneous distribution, not a cumulative counter; wrapping it in rate() (as v1/v2 did) was wrong. experimental_fuse_total_threads_ratio is intentionally omitted: it DOES report data but is constant at 16 (= --max-threads), so it carries no information. (v2 wrongly called it a dead series -- that was an instant-query sampling gap.)

panels.title: Process memory (RSS)
panels.description: Measured 80MB idle -> 617MB write -> 978MB read (12x) on a 7.8GB instance, still climbing during the read phase. Easily the most overlooked alertable signal here.

panels.title: FUSE errors by request type (app-visible failures)
panels.description: Stayed empty through the whole 2026-07-27 test: the S3 layer had transient events but Mountpoint retried every one of them, so the application saw zero errors. Any line appearing here is a genuine problem.

panels.title: Write Amplification & Waste (O_WRONLY success vs O_RDWR fail)
S3 DeleteObject rate — cleanup / wasted writes
panels.description: Sustained DeleteObject usually means writes that were created then immediately deleted. MEASURED 2026-07-28: a failed fio write test (O_RDWR, rejected by Mountpoint) produced 1470 CreateMPU+UploadPart+CompleteMPU+DeleteObject — 27k+ S3 calls, ZERO useful throughput, but still billed. A healthy O_WRONLY sequential write (593 MB/s) showed DeleteObject=0. If this line is > 0 during a pure-write workload, you are paying for create-then-delete churn.

panels.title: Write amplification — metadata reqs per UploadPart
panels.description: Ratio of metadata probes (ListObjectsV2 + HeadObject) to actual data uploads (UploadPart). Low = efficient bulk write. MEASURED: healthy seq write ~0.02 (89155 UploadPart vs ~1767 meta); failed write test ~14 (10556+10556 meta vs 1470 UploadPart) — massive metadata amplification with no data landing. Spikes here flag pathological small-file or failing-open patterns.
